chapter: On the road with Guitar Slim
title: Slim's showmanship, last records and breaking records on tour
summary: Ford describes Slim walking with his guitar, his late recordings, and the band's success in Florida, Mississippi and Alabama.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: He'd hang down from the top of the roof with his guitar and play at the same time. He made a good attraction. He was a good visual attraction. That was most of his popularity. Yeah. But he had some tunes that he sang if you listen to them. His last thing that he recorded was, If I Had My Life To Live Over. Now he died right after that. He looked into that. And another thing he did, Suffering Mind. Now that was close to Ray Charles as Ray Charles. Ray Charles heard that and got his thing from that. But Suffering Mind, I haven't heard it, but it sounds more like Ray Charles. Right now it would sound like that. It would sound like a crude Ray Charles. Because the band was playing the same type of style. Slim wasn't very sophisticated. No, he was playing, he'd come out with a red suit on, a green suit on. But he had a million selling record and the country people liked him. That's why we did our best in Florida, Mississippi, Alabama.
How did you rule? We broke records.

We broke records in Florida. Poems and Howlandale had more people there over a two week period than anybody else broke records. And he, see the people, he would come on later, we would play and he'd come on later and take off. And then we'd take intermission and then we'd play again and he'd come on. It was like a show. Yeah. Like a traveling show. Yeah, we did the warm up. Yeah. And the band was, another thing, we had a lot of good arrangements. So Lloyd did arrangement? No. No. No. No. No. No.
